executiveSummary: GM0603's official 2025 identity, generalized boundary, contained centre, 60,717 residents, 32 neighbourhoods in eleven districts, one BAG woonplaats, two BRT settlement labels and Haaglanden safety-region assignment are coherent. Published neighbourhood rows sum to 60,725 residents, eight above the municipal control (+0.013%); deterministic allocation reconciles exactly and preserves Wilhelminapark's official zero residents. All ten canonical presets run deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services with finite, bounded and reconciled results, and the web factory equals the canonical sim-core presets. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Rijswijk is a dense Delfland city whose rainfall pathway depends on street storage, separate storm sewers, groundwater, polders, pumps and the regional boezem; the municipality documents recurring water nuisance at Hoornbrug and planned sewer enlargement. The generic pluvial preset instead publishes 0.796373 legacy flood amplitude and 15,995 affected resident-equivalents at T+24 without a local rainfall, sewer, surface, pump or boezem state. A generic Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset holds 1.397206 and 29,471 affected through T+72 without naming a hydraulically connected major-river pathway, while coastal reaches 2.008562 and 29,753 at T+24 without a selected sea level, defence or connected footprint. Eight unrelated hazards reuse the same complete neighbourhood order. Official heat material identifies Plaspoelpolder as Rijswijk's largest heat island, yet it ranks 30th of 32; its roughly 20,000 jobs, more than 1,000 enterprises and 1,815 published residents also expose the missing commuter population. Only two series A4 proxy links support mobility and supply; they omit the internal station, rail/tram, Hoornbrug, street and external-care access needed operationally. Public pump, grid-planning, antenna, education and acute-care registers provide context but no complete topology, live state, backup or restoration. On the 3 September 2026 reference date, Lindelaan/Hendrik Ravesteijnplein is a dated current-project page with scheduled phases and reduced access, not a live outage feed; exact phase overlap and operating state remain Unknown. Compound service states, affected population and pressure stay exactly fixed from T+24 to T+72 despite changing forcing. Unsupported hazard, service and recovery precision must fail closed, and first-72-hour actions require authority-confirmed state, resources, valid time and expiry.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0603 official 2025 statistics, generalized geography, BAG places and neighbourhoods
evidenceSources.edition: CBS 2025; CBS/PDOK and BAG snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: The CC BY 4.0 municipality record identifies GM0603 as Rijswijk (ZH.) and reports 60,717 residents, density 4,344 per square kilometre, 20.6% aged 65 or older and 12,865 one-person households; the 2025 centre [4.324333381962232, 52.03413422162252] is inside the generalized boundary.

Thirty-two neighbourhoods in eleven districts sum to 60,725 published residents (+8, +0.013%), 29,580 households and 12,500 rounded age-65+ residents. Wilhelminapark is an observed zero-resident row, not missing data.

One active BAG woonplaats is named Rijswijk. BRT adds two settlement labels, Rijswijk (woonkern) and 't Haantje (deelkern); labels and municipality totals are different spatial/statistical concepts. Source bundle SHA-256 is 3a210bedbacc938c20251a7131974ef2507da3e179a9a5c55ec3d85f8c486c91.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Programmabegroting Rijswijk 2026–2029: water, climate, sewer and public-space programme
evidenceSources.edition: Programmabegroting 2026–2029; programme/planning evidence, not event-time operation
supports: Pages 79 and 184 say the 2021–2025 Riolerings- en Waterplan covered wastewater, rainwater, groundwater and surface water, while a new eight-year Programma Water, Klimaat en Riolering is to be made in 2026 under the Omgevingswet and reviewed after four years. The expired plan and future programme must not be merged into a current operational model without lifecycle metadata.

The budget names separate rainwater sewers and works at Volmerlaan, Visseringlaan, Kesslerpark, Lange Kleiweg, Cromvliet, Havenkwartier and ing. H.H. van Kollaan. It specifically says water nuisance often occurs at Hoornbrug and plans a larger storm sewer and public-space redesign there.

Named works and inspection-driven replacements demonstrate spatially heterogeneous sewer and pluvial mechanisms. They do not provide rainfall forcing, pipe/pump capacity, catchment connectivity, commissioning state, event-time availability or a T+72 restoration curve.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Rijswijkse Adaptatiestrategie en Aanpak voor Klimaatverandering implementation context
supports: The municipality identifies heat, heavy rain and drought as local climate pathways and says RAAK work includes an updated climate atlas, new stress tests, an Urban Waterbuffer feasibility study, risk dialogues and collaboration with Hoogheemraadschap van Delfland.

A local rainwater-discharge bylaw requires on-site storage for developments, but policy and feasibility work are not measured storage, infiltration, sewer, groundwater, subsidence or pump performance during an incident.

The page states climate-calamity-plan development stops from 2025 after a budget reversal; the first 2024 local heat plan is the last version and will not be updated annually. This is a material response-planning limitation, not proof that no other authority plan exists.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Warmteprogramma 2026 supporting appendix: cooling demand and urban heat quickscan
evidenceSources.edition: Supporting appendix published September 2025; current-condition quickscan and future scenarios remain distinct
supports: The appendix identifies four current heat islands: Bogaard stadscentrum, Plaspoelpolder, Oud-Rijswijk and Rijswijk Buiten. It calls Plaspoelpolder the municipality's largest heat island, with roughly 10–20% green and 80–90% grey surface; the quickscan reports many perceived-temperature cells at 35–41 degrees Celsius or above 41 degrees.

The document explicitly says a detailed neighbourhood heat stress test is not yet available and updated neighbourhood analyses are expected only after 2026. Quickscan maps must therefore retain coverage, method and uncertainty rather than be presented as live temperature observations.

For Plaspoelpolder the appendix describes substantial utility-building cooling demand, says no heat network is currently planned there, identifies WKO potential and discusses net congestion. This does not establish municipality-wide district-heat absence, installed WKO capacity, present grid state or cooling availability.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Public IMWA water-control assets and Delfland polder–boezem context
evidenceSources.edition: CC BY-SA 4.0 deployment snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026; partial national aggregation
supports: Point-in-polygon against the non-generalized 2025 boundary assigns 132 Delfland context points to GM0603: 17 surface-water pumps, two sluices and 113 weirs. Named pumps include Plaspoel- & Schaapweipolder, Hoge and Lage Broekpolder, Hoekpolder, Noordpolder and two A4/Prinses Beatrixlaan underdrainage records.

Capacity is null for 121 of 132 points. Eleven pump values lack a locally validated common unit/topology in the simulator; register status 'gerealiseerd' means realised in the register, not running, healthy, powered, remotely controllable or available at the exercise clock.

Delfland explains its wider managed system at https://www.hhdelfland.nl/ontdek-werk/juiste-waterpeil/omgaan-wateroverlast/waterbergingen/zoektocht-nieuwe-bergingsgebieden/vragen-antwoorden/: low polders depend on finite pumping into the boezem and conditions elsewhere can raise boezem levels. Asset points alone cannot identify Rijswijk catchments, direction, storage, groundwater, settlement, subsidence, sewer interaction, redundancy or recession.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel Haaglanden 2023 and first-72-hour resilience context
evidenceSources.edition: Regional risk profile 2023; official planning scenarios, not observation or forecast
supports: The profile places Haaglanden in former dike ring 14, treats coastal flooding as the region's most relevant large-water pathway, and separately describes primary-defence flooding, regional boezem-embankment failure and intense rainfall. Those mechanisms cannot validate one generic coast/river/pluvial scalar or an unnamed breach.

The profile treats damaging earthquake effects in Haaglanden as very unlikely/limited and regional nature-fire load as limited, while smoke and cross-boundary hazardous-material effects remain possible. This supports distinct local versus indirect pathways, not a common neighbourhood rank.

Regional plans describe cross-service dependencies and a 72-hour blackout/support-point design horizon. The 2026 pilot advice at https://www.vrh.nl/sites/default/files/2026-04/11.%20II%20Advies%20houtskoolschets%20NSP%20Haaglanden%202%20%28pilotfase%29%20AB%20VRH.pdf is governance/design evidence, not proof of an active Rijswijk support point, stock, staff, telecom, backup or guaranteed restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — NWB roads, ProRail station, scheduled public transport and time-bounded traffic context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB 1 August 2026; ProRail/OVapi snapshots 31 August–3 September 2026; NDW publication 3 September 2026 08:43Z
supports: The generated graph has only two GM0603 border edges, both series fragments of physical corridor NWB-road-4/A4: 0.726 km toward Midden-Delfland and 1.752 km toward 's-Gravenhage. Each has a 260 scenario-unit ceiling and supports only mobility and supply; neither is independent physical capacity or a complete evacuation route set.

One ProRail station named Rijswijk and 89 spatially contained OVapi stop areas are map/schedule context. The GTFS feed covers 30 August–12 December 2026 but has no disaster-time vehicle position, occupancy, capacity, staff, power, track, tram, bridge, tunnel or restoration state.

The deployed NDW current-picture snapshot was published at 08:43Z and retrieved at 08:44Z on 3 September 2026; zero point-assigned GM0603 matches is a bounded no-match, not proof that A4, local streets, Hoornbrug, railway, tram or care routes were open. Observed/replay state must never be silently applied to a synthetic scenario clock.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public acute-care, grid-planning, antenna and education context
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026; public planning/register snapshots retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: No questionnaire-listed emergency department lies in GM0603. From the municipal reference point, the nearest RIVM records are Reinier de Graaf Delft (4.217 km), HMC Westeinde (4.718 km) and Haga Leyweg (4.834 km), all reporting 24/7 emergency and acute-obstetric service. Straight-line distance and dated role do not establish ambulance time, route access, acceptance, staffing, occupancy or backup endurance.

One NBNL sample at postcode 2287TK maps to Stedin service area Treubstraat: withdrawal/injection capacity fields are null, both queues and unique requests are published zero, eleven projects are listed and earliest project year is 2026. This single large-user planning lookup is not municipal topology, current household availability or an outage/recovery feed.

RDI assigns 86 registered antenna installations: 41 mobile-communication, 15 fixed-link, one broadcast, two other-mobile and 27 radio-amateur records. DUO assigns 49 education locations. Neither register supplies event-time occupancy, coverage, operator/backhaul, power/backup, shelter/care role, supplies or operating state.

evidenceSources.title: E09 — Lindelaan/Hendrik Ravesteijnplein works and Plaspoelpolder activity context
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal pages inspected on reference date 3 September 2026; page issue/update timestamp not exposed
supports: The page says new gas and water lines and sewer have been installed and the parking-area project is nearly complete. It schedules phase 2 from 10 August for six weeks and phase 3 to begin in September for five weeks; homes and shops remain accessible, with reduced parking and phase-3 foot access.

At 3 September 2026, calendar arithmetic places phase 2 within its stated six-week window, while phase 3 has only a month-level start and may overlap. The page lacks an issue/update timestamp, exact phase-3 start/end, completion confirmation and real-time road/utility state; therefore the strongest semantics are planned/current-project context with bounded schedule and Unknown operating state, not live outage or closure telemetry.

The municipality's https://www.rijswijk.nl/plaspoelpolder page describes a 126-hectare work/live area with more than 1,000 enterprises and about 20,000 jobs across offices, ICT, services, trade and industry. CBS publishes only 1,815 residents but 1,505 businesses for the Plaspoelpolder neighbourhood, so resident-only demand misses a large, time-varying commuter cohort; the figures do not specify event-time occupancy.

identity.summary: Official code, name, province, safety region, editions, centre and headline demography agree.
notes: Feature id, collection code and regional-bundle code are GM0603; the official display name is Rijswijk (ZH.), province Zuid-Holland and safety region Haaglanden.
The reference point lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary, and the municipality belongs to exactly one generated safety region.
Annual identity/statistics, 2026 project pages, near-real-time observations and the synthetic exercise clock retain separate editions and valid times.

geography.summary: The 2025 generalized geometry is coherent, but water, heat, infrastructure and activity require full spatial mechanisms.
notes: Thirty-two neighbourhood label points, one BAG woonplaats and two BRT settlement labels load without a generated boundary flag.

Delfland polders, boezem, pumps, sewers, groundwater and surface flow cross administrative and neighbourhood boundaries; a label point or municipality scalar cannot identify connectivity, arrival, depth or recession.
Generalized polygons do not resolve buildings, roads, bridge/tunnel portals, land/water, elevation, shade, paving, heat exposure, industrial parcels or model NoData.

demography.summary: Official 2025 control totals agree and neighbourhood rounding/zero semantics are explicit.
notes: Population is 60,717, density 4,344, age65Pct 20.6 and one-person households 12,865; neighbourhood rows sum to 60,725 (+8), households to 29,580 and rounded age65+ counts to 12,500.

Stervoorde has 7,510 residents including 2,190 rounded age65+; Overvoorde has 470 residents including 375 rounded age65+. These aggregate vulnerability signals are not household/care dependency or individual location.

Plaspoelpolder's roughly 20,000 jobs versus 1,815 published residents demonstrates material time-varying commuter demand absent from the resident control. Visitors, pupils, patients, carers and household preparedness are not observed.

regionalDetail.summary: Core neighbourhood fields are complete, while socioeconomic, district-heat, water and operational coverage is partial.
notes: All 32 rows have population, age, household, business, land/water and density fields. Home value/housing/tenure and benefit fields are available for 28/32, household size and doctor/supermarket distance for 31/32, and cars per household for 26/32.
District-heating percentage and public-charging-point count have 0/32 coverage. Null means unavailable in this CBS table, not zero networks, connections or demand.
HWH assets, the one NBNL postcode sample, RDI antennas, DUO locations and RIVM hospitals are context-only and `affectsSimulation=false`; none establishes full topology or current service.

settlements.summary: Rijswijk and 't Haantje settlement identities are coherent but carry no event-time population or capacity.
notes: The active BAG woonplaats is Rijswijk; BRT contains the Rijswijk woonkern and 't Haantje deelkern.
Settlement labels are cartographic context, not replacements for the municipal CBS population or neighbourhood allocation.
No source gives event-time resident, commuter, visitor, patient, pupil, reception or self-reliance counts by settlement.

transport.summary: A4, station and scheduled transit context are reproducible, but the two-link graph cannot represent local first-72-hour reachability.
notes: Both logical edges are A4 series fragments on one physical corridor toward Midden-Delfland and 's-Gravenhage; ceilings are non-additive scenario units.

Rijswijk station and 89 OVapi stop areas are present, while internal roads, tram/rail state, Hoornbrug, low crossings/tunnels, station access, care destinations and alternate routes are absent from the flow graph.

The municipal works page provides planned access restrictions with incomplete phase timing; the NDW snapshot has no GM0603 point match. Neither proves route openness, utility availability or emergency throughput.

emergencyContext.summary: Haaglanden hazards and 72-hour governance are relevant, but local resources, actions and external-care access are unverified.
notes: The regional profile supports storm, coastal/regional-water, pluvial, heat, winter, cyber/utility, smoke and cross-boundary dependencies while treating damaging local earthquake and nature fire as limited.
No RIVM-listed emergency department lies inside GM0603; three nearest reference-point facilities are external and route/acceptance dependent.

RAAK climate-calamity-plan development was stopped from 2025, and the regional support-point concept remains a pilot/design. No reviewed source confirms Rijswijk action state, support-point activation, staff, stock, generator fuel, water, telecom or completion.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets produce complete deterministic outputs at six checkpoints for all eight services; physical validity fails separately.
notes: `MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0603 pnpm audit:model` passed one file/two tests over severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

A focused runtime probe confirms every UI `createScenario` object byte-matches `createScenarioConfig` for all ten ids. Affected population and person-hours are model proxies, not observed people, casualties, evacuees or customer outage-hours.

numericalInvariants.summary: Bounds, determinism, ledger closure, route ceilings and local reconciliation pass on the audited build.
notes: Hazard/service values are finite and bounded; affected population is integral and within 0..60,717; repeat T+24 snapshots are byte-identical; service ledgers/counterfactuals close; cumulative person-hours are monotone.

At compound T+24 all 32 official neighbourhoods and exactly 60,717 allocated residents reconcile for every service. Maximum displayed population/affected error is zero and maximum demand/delivery reconciliation error in the focused probe is 2.13e-14 / 7.11e-15.

Wilhelminapark retains zero allocated residents. Its small non-residential activity-weight demand remains separately explicit rather than turning 0/0 into a failure; this is modelled context, not observed live demand.

Only mobility and supply expose the two local A4 logical-proxy route records, and each sampled flow stays below its scenario-unit effective capacity. Numerical correctness does not establish local calibration.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Flood, heat and local exposure do not follow Rijswijk's mechanism-specific geography.
notes: River T+24 through T+72 holds severity 0.430941 and legacy flood amplitude 1.397206 without a named major river, defence state, boundary hydrograph, connected footprint or recession.

Coastal T+24 reaches severity 0.613607, amplitude 2.008562 and 29,753 affected without selected sea level/datum, wind field, primary-defence/breach/overtopping state, arrival or local inundation layer.

Pluvial T+24 reaches amplitude 0.796373 although Rijswijk evidence instead distinguishes named sewer works, Hoornbrug nuisance, local storage/infiltration, polders, pumps and the boezem. No rainfall hyetograph or hydraulic state selects those pathways.

Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire have the exact same complete 32-neighbourhood order: Vrijenban, Stervoorde, Stationskwartier, Sion and Welgelegen lead. Plaspoelpolder, the documented largest heat island, ranks 30th.

serviceDependencies.summary: Service equations are inspectable, but exact utility, mobility, care and supply states exceed public evidence.
notes: Compound T+24 availability is power 0.175050, water 0.287897, drainage 0.166604, gas 0.450741, telecom 0.128898, mobility 0.884559, facilities 0.215475 and supply 0.820673. No operator validates these local fractions, dependencies, backup windows or repair curves.
The graph correctly restricts NWB edges to mobility and supply, but two A4 edges cannot represent internal/alternate road, bridge, tunnel, tram/rail, hospital, depot, repair or delivery reachability.

HWH pumps/weirs, a single Stedin planning sample, RDI antennas, municipal gas/water/sewer works, null district-heat fields, external RIVM hospitals and DUO sites do not provide safe-to-publish causal topology, current state, pressure/quality, backhaul, stock, staff, fuel or switching.

Power, drinking water, wastewater/drainage, gas, district heat, telecom, facilities and supply must expose evidence class and Unknown state independently; provider territory or a realised/planned point is not connectivity or availability.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic traceability passes, while missing hazard-source and operating-state dimensions remain hidden behind precise output.
notes: Hazard contributions, service availability, system pressure and counterfactual deltas reconcile exactly under the declared synthetic equations.

Derived-screening river/coastal values do not disclose a source water body, level/datum, defence state, hydraulic footprint, arrival/recession, resolution, coverage or NoData mask. A field named `floodDepthM` is unsupported as local forecast metres.

Official registers, scheduled works, planning projects, observed NDW messages, authority scenarios and synthetic presets have distinct evidence classes, issue times, valid windows and expiry. The current UI/output contract cannot establish those distinctions for every causal value.
Cyber has no named target/attack path; first-72-hour interventions have no proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled state or responsible-authority/resource ledger.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 plateaus, recovery labels and first-72-hour actions are not supported by hydraulic or operator evidence.
notes: River retains amplitude 1.397206, 29,471 affected and pressure 0.484520 at T+72 while person-hours rise to 2,180,164.540; no selected high-water, defence, pump or recession evidence supports this curve.

Coastal physical forcing clears by T+72 but 11,585 affected, pressure 0.275435 and 2,235,673.769 person-hours remain with a recovering label; no dewatering, access, repair or facility evidence validates that state.

Compound retains amplitude 0.822149, 41,159 affected, pressure 0.621149 and all eight service availabilities exactly unchanged from T+24 to T+72 while cyber forcing declines and person-hours rise to 2,872,947.558.

A regional 72-hour design horizon, household guidance, a works schedule or planning project cannot prove action completion, aid arrival, route clearance, hospital acceptance, household stock, utility restoration or all-clear.

findings.summary: Official identity, small neighbourhood rounding and zero-resident semantics reconcile correctly.
findings.evidence: E01 gives 60,717 municipal residents and 60,725 summed neighbourhood residents (+8, +0.013%). The focused allocation returns exactly 60,717 for every service and keeps Wilhelminapark at zero residents while separating any modelled non-residential demand.
findings.action: Keep the municipal CBS record as the population control, preserve every published neighbourhood value/null, document deterministic rounding reconciliation and retain regression coverage for exact zero versus missing versus non-residential activity.

findings.summary: Major-river and coastal presets publish precise direct inundation without a selected connected hydraulic event.
findings.evidence: E06 distinguishes coastal/primary-defence and regional-water pathways. The model instead holds an unnamed Rhine/Meuse/IJssel amplitude of 1.397206 and 29,471 affected through T+72, while coastal reaches 2.008562 and 29,753 at T+24. Neither selects source water, boundary condition/datum, defence/breach state, footprint, arrival or recession.
findings.action: Fail closed on direct GM0603 depth and affected-population claims until an authority-selected, versioned hydraulic scenario proves source connectivity and supplies boundary condition, defence state, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, resolution, licence, coverage, NoData and expert approval. Keep major-river, coastal, regional-boezem/dyke and pluvial labels separate.

findings.evidence: E02 documents separate storm sewers, recurring Hoornbrug nuisance and named capacity projects; E03 adds storage/infiltration and an Urban Waterbuffer study; E05 assigns named polder pumps. Yet T+24 publishes 0.796373 legacy amplitude and drainage 0.345861 without a rain hyetograph, terrain/imperviousness, sewer/pump capacity and state, groundwater, storage, boezem level or catchment connectivity.
findings.action: Build a governed pluvial adapter from a versioned municipal/provincial rain stress test, AHN/BGT flow/storage surfaces, sewer/groundwater evidence and Delfland catchment/pump/boezem states. Until coverage and units are explicit, render local depth, exposure and drainage recovery Unknown instead of exact.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated hazards reuse one neighbourhood ranking and contradict the official heat hotspot.
findings.evidence: The focused T+24 probe gives the same full order for storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire, led by Vrijenban, Stervoorde, Stationskwartier, Sion and Welgelegen. E04 identifies Plaspoelpolder as Rijswijk's largest heat island, but the model ranks it 30th of 32. One seed cannot encode drainage, defence, heat, wind, snow, cyber target and smoke mechanisms.
findings.action: Remove the shared seed from causal spatial claims. Use hazard-specific source/footprint fields for hydraulic, rainfall, heat/land cover, wind, winter, fire/smoke and explicit cyber/service zones, or render uniform/Unknown. Add cross-hazard rank-diversity and documented-hotspot tests with coverage/NoData.

findings.summary: Heat and service demand omit documented hotspots and large commuter/care-sensitive cohorts.
findings.evidence: E04 identifies four heat islands, with Plaspoelpolder's 80–90% grey surface and high utility-building cooling demand; E09 reports about 20,000 jobs and more than 1,000 firms there versus 1,815 CBS residents. E01 also shows high aggregate age65+ concentrations. The heat preset uses resident/static context, reports 4,079 affected at T+24 and zero at T+72 despite continuing heat/drought forcing, without occupancy, indoor heat or care dependency.
findings.action: Keep resident control separate from time-indexed commuters, visitors, pupils, patients and care/support cohorts. Integrate versioned heat/PET/land-cover coverage when available, building/indoor vulnerability and explicitly sourced occupancy ranges; never add overlapping populations. Treat the 2025 quickscan as context until the post-2026 detailed analysis is governed.

findings.summary: Two A4 border links cannot support local evacuation, bridge/tunnel, transit, repair or external acute-care claims.
findings.evidence: E07 gives one station, 89 scheduled stop areas and two non-additive A4 series links; E09 gives a current-project access restriction but not live state. E08 places the nearest three listed 24/7 acute-care destinations outside GM0603 at 4.217–4.834 km straight-line. The model has no internal road/rail/tram, Hoornbrug, tunnel/underpass, destination, ambulance, occupancy or acceptance nodes.
findings.action: Build a multimodal, time-dependent internal/cross-boundary reachability graph from NWB/BGT, ProRail, GTFS and authoritative crossing geometry. Use NDW only in issue/valid-time-aligned observed/replay mode; keep route passability, vehicle/staff, evacuation throughput and hospital acceptance Unknown without confirmation.

findings.summary: Exact power, water, drainage, gas, district-heat, telecom, facility and supply values are not locally calibrated.
findings.evidence: Compound T+24 publishes exact availabilities 0.128898–0.884559. E05's 132 assets have 121 null capacities and no governed hydraulic topology/state. E08's one Treubstraat grid-planning lookup, 86 antenna records, 49 schools and external hospitals are `affectsSimulation=false`; E02/E09 utility works prove neither outage nor commissioning. District-heat statistics are null in all 32 rows, not zero.
findings.action: Expose each service as an aggregate synthetic dependency proxy unless operator-approved evidence supplies safe zones, state, units, backup and restoration ranges. Separate potable quantity/quality/advisory, wastewater and surface-water control. Preserve unavailable/security-sensitive topology as Unknown and attach evidence class, publisher, time, completeness, topology semantics and `affectsSimulation`.

findings.summary: Compound T+24–T+72 plateau and recovery labels lack forcing, operator and action evidence.
findings.evidence: Compound keeps flood amplitude 0.822149, 41,159 affected, pressure 0.621149 and all eight service fractions exactly fixed from T+24 to T+72 although cyber forcing declines; person-hours reach 2,872,947.558. River/coastal residuals likewise lack selected recession/dewatering. E03/E06 provide planning horizons but no local action, stock, crew, acceptance, repair or completion feed.
findings.action: Replace automatic plateaus/recovery with event-specific persistence plus authority/operator-confirmed actions and restoration ranges. At every checkpoint expose remaining forcing, unresolved inputs, service state, affected equivalents, matched-baseline burden, proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled actions, owner, resources, issue/valid time and expiry.

findings.summary: Planned municipal works and bounded observations can be misread as live scenario operating state.
findings.evidence: E09 schedules phase 2 from 10 August for six weeks and phase 3 only as starting in September for five weeks. On 3 September phase 2 is calendar-active but the page does not timestamp its own issue/update, give exact phase-3 dates or confirm field state. E07's NDW snapshot is observed at 08:43Z and has no local point match. Neither applies to an arbitrary synthetic exercise clock.
findings.action: Implement explicit synthetic, planned/project, observed, replay and forecast modes. Store publisher, retrieved/issued/valid/expiry times, phase precision, location match and confidence. Expire stale records; never let a schedule, page tense, project completion claim or absent incident match assert current road/utility operation.

findings.summary: True zero, null, no local point, out-of-coverage and not-applicable states need distinct rendering.
findings.evidence: Wilhelminapark has official zero residents; the Treubstraat sample has published zero queued requests but null capacity; district heat/charging are null in 32/32; no local RIVM SEH, KNMI station/event, PM2.5 station, RWS Waterinfo point or NDW situation is assigned; 121 water assets have null capacity. These states do not mean no people at event time, no congestion, no network, no hazard, safe roads or normal service.
findings.action: Use a shared UI/API/export state contract: measured or modelled value including zero, Unknown/not covered, stale/expired, and not applicable. Show publisher, edition, issue/valid/retrieval/expiry time, unit, coverage/completeness, licence, confidence and `affectsSimulation`; prevent null/no-match from receiving safe colours or zero labels.

findings.summary: Storm, winter, cyber, earthquake, wildfire/smoke and compound are bounded stress tests, not local forecasts.
findings.evidence: E06 supports severe weather and cyber/lifeline relevance, low damaging-earthquake relevance and limited nature-fire load. The model nevertheless applies generic curves: winter T+24 severity 0.791952, cyber 0.517546 without target, earthquake peak 0.006612 without selected KNMI event/site response, and wildfire 0 direct flame but 0.230515 smoke. E09's mixed Plaspoelpolder trade/industry adds context but no industrial-release scenario.
findings.action: Retain visibly synthetic exercises with editable parameters and uncertainty. Require valid-time KNMI inputs for observed/replay/forecast weather or seismic modes, a named cyber target/path, eligible fire source/perimeter/fuel/wind/plume and authority-led industrial source term before direct consequences. Disclose hazards outside the ten-preset suite.

findings.summary: The focused deterministic and reconciliation contract passes for GM0603 on the audited build.
findings.evidence: The required gate passes two tests over 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services. Focused reproduction confirms UI/core preset equality, finite/bounded values, deterministic T+24 replay, causal/counterfactual closure, monotone burden, exact 32-neighbourhood/60,717-person and demand/delivery reconciliation, service-layer-invariant local hazard, zero-resident preservation and bounded logical route flow.
findings.action: Retain the focused gate in CI and add release regressions for hydraulic source contracts, mechanism-specific neighbourhood allocation, heat hotspot/dynamic cohorts, internal reachability, live-mode expiry, Unknown/NoData rendering and evidence-supported recovery/actions.

corrections.summary: Fail closed on unsupported GM0603 major-river/coastal precision and bind every water hazard to a distinct source/defence/hydraulic contract.
corrections.validation: Before correction, river reports 1.397206 and 29,471 affected through T+72 and coastal reports 2.008562/29,753 at T+24. Require explicit major-river, coast/primary defence, regional-boezem/dyke and pluvial source classes; compatible source water, boundary condition/datum, defence state, footprint, arrival/recession, units, scenario class, resolution, licence, coverage, NoData and expert approval; unsupported direct values remain neutral/Unknown.

corrections.validation: Eight unrelated hazards must no longer share one 32-neighbourhood order. Versioned municipal/provincial rain and heat coverage plus Delfland catchment data must recover documented mechanism areas such as Hoornbrug and Plaspoelpolder or show Unknown. Test service-layer invariance, coverage masks, tie handling and source containment independently.

corrections.summary: Add non-additive dynamic population and internal multimodal/external-care reachability without fabricating operation.
corrections.validation: Resident totals stay exactly 60,717 while explicitly sourced commuter/visitor/pupil/patient/care cohorts remain separate, time-indexed and non-overlapping. Internal road/bridge/tunnel/rail/tram and destination routing exposes static versus observed state; straight-line RIVM distance, schedule data and two A4 links never assert ambulance access, evacuation throughput or acceptance.

corrections.validation: NWB remains only mobility/supply proxy; HWH, NBNL, RDI, DUO, RIVM and project pages remain `affectsSimulation=false` unless a governed adapter supplies service-specific zones/state, units, capacity, backup and recovery. Preserve null capacity, scoped planning zero, no local point and security-sensitive topology as Unknown, with potable/wastewater/surface-water and district-heat semantics separated.

corrections.summary: Add evidence lifecycle, Unknown/NoData UI and authority-confirmed first-72-hour action/recovery ledgers.
corrections.validation: Synthetic, planned/project, observed, replay and forecast modes expose source, issue/valid/retrieval/expiry time, location match, uncertainty and `affectsSimulation`. Lindelaan phase wording cannot become live closure; empty NDW cannot become open road. Each checkpoint shows forcing, services, affected equivalents, matched-baseline burden and proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled actions with owner/resources; no action or restoration is inferred.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI, RWS/WMCN, Delfland, VRH, municipality, utility or hospital forecast, warning, probability estimate, evacuation instruction, casualty model or restoration promise.

No expert-selected coast, major-river, primary/regional-defence or Delfland polder/boezem event supplies boundary level/hydrograph and datum, defence state, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, verified unit, probability, uncertainty or NoData for GM0603.
The legacy `floodDepthM` field is derived-screening/synthetic output and cannot be read as surveyed, forecast or authority-approved local metres.

The 2026 sewer budget names problems and projects but not current commissioning, rain forcing, pipe/pump capacity, catchment connectivity, groundwater, infiltration, overflow, damage, power dependency or incident recovery.

The 132 HWH points are a partial register; 121 null capacities, eleven unvalidated capacity values and realised status do not establish compatible units, connectivity, operation, redundancy, backup, storage, pumping head or recession.

Groundwater level, salinity, land subsidence/settlement and their interaction with sewers, roads, foundations and drought are not ingested; lack of a reviewed calibrated layer remains Unknown, not no pathway.

The Rijswijk heat material is a current-condition quickscan/supporting programme document and explicitly lacks detailed neighbourhood analysis until after 2026; it is not a live temperature observation or individual health-risk map.

CBS values are rounded/suppressed annual residential context. Commuters, visitors, pupils, patients, institutional/care residents at event time, household stocks and people needing assisted evacuation are not measured or safely inferred.

Plaspoelpolder's about 20,000 jobs is a general municipal area figure, not a simultaneous occupancy count; its trade/industry mix does not establish hazardous inventories, source terms, protective zones or an active industrial incident.

The two A4 records are series sections of one logical physical corridor and scenario capacity is non-additive; local streets, alternate roads, bridge/tunnel/underpass portals, rail/tram, walking/cycling, fuel, control and clearance are absent.
ProRail and GTFS geometry/schedules do not establish event-time train, tram or bus running, station accessibility, power/signalling, vehicle occupancy, staffing, capacity or recovery.

The 3 September 2026 Lindelaan/Hendrik Ravesteijnplein page lacks its own issue/update time, exact phase-3 dates and field confirmation. Its schedule is project context and must expire independently of observed operating state.
Zero point-assigned NDW records in one 08:43Z current-picture snapshot is not evidence that every GM0603 road/crossing is open, nor can it be projected into a synthetic future exercise.

No in-boundary RIVM emergency department is a dataset result, not no local care or need. External hospital role and straight-line distance do not establish travel time, access, acceptance, occupancy, staff, generator fuel or transfer capacity.

One Treubstraat NBNL sample is large-user planning context. Published queue zero is scoped; null capacity and eleven projects do not establish municipal power/gas topology, present load, outage, switching, backup or restoration.

RDI antenna installations do not establish operator, coverage, traffic, backhaul, power/battery, congestion, damage, availability or recovery; exact reuse licence was not stated in the WFS capabilities.

District-heating percentage and public charging are missing from all 32 CBS rows. The Plaspoelpolder statement that no warmtenet is currently planned is area-specific; neither state proves municipality-wide zero installed heat infrastructure or service.

No complete public drinking-water pressure/quality, gas pressure district, electricity feeder/switching, telecom backhaul, municipal sewer, facility backup, stocked supply or operator restoration topology is authorized in the simulator.

The regional support-point and 72-hour concepts are preparedness/governance horizons. No reviewed Rijswijk site, activation, accessibility, stock, staff, generator fuel, water, telecom, aid arrival or action completion feed is available.

RAAK's stopped climate-calamity-plan development and non-annually updated heat plan are municipal programme facts, not absence of all VRH/operator plans; plan existence never proves exercise-time activation or resource availability.

Earthquake uses a fixed Groningen source without a selected valid-time event/site-response surface; wildfire uses remote smoke and no local flame; cyber has no named target, architecture or attack/containment path; winter/storm lack locally selected KNMI forcing.

Event-attributable service person-hours is a matched-model weighted availability proxy, not customer outage-hours, illness, casualties, displacement or welfare loss. Six-hour checkpoints can miss rapid changes and 72 hours excludes prolonged dewatering, contamination and reconstruction.
